proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer cannot tell whether DRAM or the L1/TEX pipe is the truly saturated memory unit, nor what limits occupancy at 62-89% — so it cannot choose between cutting DRAM bytes, widening accesses to cut L1 wavefronts, or adding warps versus per-thread ILP.

rationale.l1tex__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustai: HIGH (>= DRAM %) -> L1/TEX wavefront-bound: vectorize to 128-bit loads/stores, use contiguous aligned blocks, drop masked/gathered accesses to cut sectors per byte / LOW (<< DRAM ~92%) -> DRAM is the true roofline: only reduce total bytes (fuse read passes, avoid re-reads, in-place stores, smaller dtypes); otherwise keep the simple streaming pattern to avoid the 0.1-0.6x regressions
rationale.launch__occupancy_limit_registers: HIGH/binding (with warps_active<85% and DRAM<90%) -> occupancy is register-capped: shrink per-thread register footprint (smaller tiles, less unrolling, tune num_warps) to fit more warps and raise loads-in-flight / LOW/not binding -> registers are free: spend them on per-thread MLP (wider vectors, multiple independent loads, double-buffered tiles) instead of adding warps

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:The L2 hit-rate cut at ~46% sits at the natural hit-vs-miss crossover—a real cache regime—and causally explains the long-scoreboard stall split (misses to DRAM drive memory-latency stalls), whereas candidate 2's absolute DRAM-bytes threshold is input-size dependent and candidate 0's 19% SM-throughput cut is an arbitrary low-utilization point with no clean hardware boundary.
